rv.q: It’s a warm introduction to a new writing team, as well as the perfect calling card to prospective producers and directors.
Space Dogs is a clever show - unique in its concept and execution, carefully straddling the line between absurd and moving, satirical and serious, and overall charming.
In short, it is a smashing way to spend an evening.
40-odd dogs paid the fare, and Space Dogs is their daft, heartfelt requiem.
This is an enjoyable show performed by two very talented and likeable performers, but it is somewhat protracted, and I’m not sure who their target market is in this current format.
Space Dogs can feel sometimes like watching two different shows, but the writers manage to balance the family-friendly with the introspective when it comes to the dogs themselves.
What could easily have felt like a novelty instead becomes an incredibly smart and well executed piece of theatre.
This is one mission well worth boarding.
The writing and musicianship create a theatrical collision unlike anything I have seen before.
I left entertained and thinking more about the human (and canine) stories that sit behind history.
A funny and surprisingly moving tribute to the canine cosmonauts.
With engaging performances and some clever staging, it's an entertaining piece of theatre.
Despite its shortcomings, Space Dogs is barking mad of a concept, but instead of delivering a committed bite, it served a more of a playful nibble.
This is a clever show, but probably needs re-casting with guys twenty years younger than Blaemire and Hughes to have any future.
Space Dogs is a charming, inventive and entertaining musical that transforms an extraordinary chapter of space history into an engaging theatrical experience.

cn.t: Critics find this quirky rock musical about Soviet space dogs surprisingly moving and entertaining, praising its inventive energy and humor, though some note it feels more like a TED Talk with music than traditional theatre.
